muskingum_cunge.coefficient_evaluation_note: coefficients are hydraulically derived per section but FROZEN at the policy reference state (the (Q0+Q1)/2 midpoint of the dry-start transition); they are not updated per routing step. Flow dependence enters through the per-member reference-flow perturbations.

correlation_note: members are whole physically consistent worlds: the upper (slow, lossy) member pairs high roughness with a low evaluation flow, high seepage, and a larger surveyed channel. The seepage-rate perturbation widens the LOSS band only; in-cascade state threading always uses the nominal seepage estimate so a perturbed loss band cannot exhaust the evaluation flow. The loss denominator stays at the nominal element reference flow; capacity is a degenerate planning ceiling so no member can relax the overload check (policy section 6).

unavailable_reasons.geometry_unavailable: no authoritative cross-section, roughness, slope, or rating exists for this span and the engineering-prior policy forbids invented geometry (LMC 0+000-0+170 outlet flume)
unavailable_reasons.conveyance_loss_exceeds_reference: the approved seepage policy derives a conveyance loss that reaches or exceeds the reference flow for this reach; the reach is explicitly unavailable rather than shipping a non-physical response
unavailable_reasons.hydraulic_state_unavailable: the approved policy cannot derive an admissible reference hydraulic state or a stable response for this reach from the surveyed evidence; the reach is explicitly unavailable rather than extrapolating the channel
